subject.title: [Bug]: In msteams channel messages, OpenClaw can't access inbound attachments

question: Should Microsoft Teams Graph media fallback be default-off and config-gated for group/channel messages, or should OpenClaw attempt it by default whenever non-personal Teams messages have HTML but no resolved media?
rationale: Current main intentionally avoids Graph calls without extracted attachment IDs to prevent mention-only noise, but the issue and linked live evidence show Teams can strip those IDs from real file uploads; this is a product/compatibility tradeoff, not just a mechanical code fix.

options.title: Config-gated opt-in
options.body: Land a default-off Graph media fallback setting so existing deployments keep current behavior unless operators accept the extra Graph lookup cost and permissions.

options.title: Default Graph fallback
options.body: Attempt Graph fetches by default for non-personal Teams messages that have HTML but no resolved media, accepting extra Graph calls to reduce setup friction.

options.title: Keep current gate
options.body: Leave the behavior unchanged and document that some Teams channel/group file uploads are unreadable when Bot Framework strips attachment IDs.

recommendation.title: Config-gated opt-in
recommendation.body: Land a default-off Graph media fallback setting so existing deployments keep current behavior unless operators accept the extra Graph lookup cost and permissions.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the broadest recent msteams ownership signal and is the best available owner for the config/default tradeoff.
